display.title: Episode 447: Reb Boruch and the Hidden Tzaddik (Before Sukkos)
display.summary_short: Before Sukkos, Uncle Yossi explains the holy 'shadow of faith' of the sukkah, and tells how the Shpoler Zeide's birth was foretold by a hidden tzaddik.
display.summary_long: Broadcast a few days before Sukkos 5751. Uncle Yossi explains that after Yom Kippur we start building the sukkah right away, and that the sukkah is a mitzvah that surrounds the whole person. The Zohar calls it the 'shadow of faith', and each night the Ushpizin, from Avraham Avinu to Dovid HaMelech, visit us. The easiest way to beautify the sukkah is a real smile, and he urges children to invite friends who have no sukkah. After the Hakochainik march, story time: Reb Boruch, a generous man who ran a free guest house and even swapped tired horses for fresh ones, welcomes a plainly dressed traveler and his wife. On Shabbos night he sees a brilliant light from the guest's room, peeks through the keyhole, and sees the guest saying Tikkun Chatzos beside a figure dressed in white. Between the two halves of the story, a second-grade class from a Brooklyn girls' school recites the Shema and everyone gives tzedakah. The hidden tzaddik reveals that the figure was the Maharal of Prague, and blesses Reb Boruch with a son who will carry the Maharal's soul: Aryeh Leib, the future Shpoler Zeide. The show ends with an invitation to the Sukkos Experience fair.
display.lesson: Do mitzvos with joy and welcome guests warmly; you never know who your guest really is.

date.note: A few days before Sukkos, which begins 'Wednesday night'; 'this coming Sunday, October 7th' is the second day of Chol HaMoed. Tuesday before = 13 Tishrei 5751.

advisories.note: The Maharal's soul is said to return to the world in the Shpoler Zeide (gilgul).

privacy.note: The visiting class's teacher is named on air.

sources_cited.note: The sukkah is called 'tzila dimeheimnusa', the shadow of faith.
